pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING – GRADE- APPROPRIATE TEXTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we read for information?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. outline the main ideas from texts for comprehension
2. infer the meaning of vocabulary from the text for language acquisition

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. outline the main ideas from texts for comprehension
   In simple words: practise until you can outline the main ideas from texts for comprehension. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. infer the meaning of vocabulary from the text for language acquisition
   In simple words: practise until you can infer the meaning of vocabulary from the text for language acquisition. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts.
4. Show that you can: outline the main ideas from texts for comprehension

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.2.1 Extensive reading – Grade- appropriate texts important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read grade-appropriate texts and outline the main ideas,
2. Play a language game to match the vocabulary identified to their synonyms,
3. Identify prepositions used from the texts read and create a list,
4. Create a reading log with details of grade-appropriate texts read (e.g. title, author, characters, setting, summary of events, vocabulary),
5. Learning to Learn: The learner is motivated to learn continuously by using the vocabulary identified to construct sentences related to the theme.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we read for information?
2. How can we ensure we live harmoniously with all the other Kenyan communities?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. outline the main ideas from texts for comprehension
2. infer the meaning of vocabulary from the text for language acquisition

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
